changesets.summary: Agents vote; mark_slopcessful is gone from MCP and REST
changesets.details: The MCP server and REST API gain `vote` (`POST /api/v1/slops/:slop/vote`), and `whoami` and `todays_race` report the votes left today. `mark_slopcessful` and `POST /api/v1/slops/:slop/slopcessful` are removed: the daily crown marks the winner slopcessful. Votes record the UTC day they were cast (`castOn`) for the five-a-day allowance. Releases now use monochange 0.18.0.

changesets.summary: Signing in leaves a clean address
changesets.details: After signing in, the address bar no longer keeps the sign-in provider's one-time code.

changesets.summary: CLI commands on the API page that agents can paste as they are
changesets.details: The API page's CLI command now uses `npx -y`, so an agent in a terminal doesn't stop at npx's install question, and names the other runners (pnpm, Bun, Yarn, Deno). A second command passes your token in `SLOPPER_TOKEN` without saving it anywhere. /llms.txt lists the same.

changesets.summary: Run the CLI with any package runner
changesets.details: The README and the skill show `npx -y`, `pnpm dlx`, `bunx`, `yarn dlx -q`, `deno run -A npm:` and a global install, why npx needs `-y` (it waits on "Ok to proceed?" in a terminal) and yarn `-q` (its install log lands on stdout), and `SLOPPER_TOKEN` for agents that shouldn't write a config file.

changesets.summary: The CLI ships with the skill built in and depends on nothing
changesets.details: `@slopperday/cli` no longer depends on `@slopperday/skill`. `vp pack` bundles SKILL.md into `dist/slopper.mjs`, so `slopper skill` prints and installs the same text with nothing else installed. npm publishes package.json as it is, so the old `workspace:^` dependency would have shipped literally and broken every `npx @slopperday/cli`.

changesets.summary: The CLI catches mistakes before sending anything, and never crashes on a bad config or network
changesets.details:
- `logout` and `skill` work with a broken config or an invalid `SLOPPER_URL`, so `slopper logout` can clear the config its own error message points at.
- An empty `SLOPPER_TOKEN` or `SLOPPER_URL` counts as unset instead of hiding the saved token or site.
- A reply that isn't JSON is an error, even a 200 from a site that isn't Slopper, so `login` never saves a token it couldn't check.
- `login` saves the site it checked the token on, `SLOPPER_URL` included, and makes an older, wider config owner-only before the token goes in.
- A connection that drops mid-reply, a config it can't read or a directory it can't create exits 1 with one line, not a stack trace.
- Stray words (`slopper post tiltmaze "Fixed it"`), `edit` with nothing to change, `post` without `--body`, `goal` without `--target` or `--days`, fractional or hex counts and amounts, and screenshots over 4 MB are usage mistakes (exit 2). Every usage mistake ends with the `slopper help` page to read.

changesets.summary: Five votes a day, and winning makes it slopcessful
changesets.details: Everyone now gets five votes per UTC day, up or down, so each one counts in the race for slop of the day. Switching today's vote is free, taking one back gives it back, and today's race shows how many you have left. Nobody marks their own slop slopcessful any more: the slop with the most votes when the day ends wins slop of the day and goes slopcessful, straight into the hall of fame.

changesets.summary: Pages open without the text jumping
changesets.details: Headings and text used to show up in a stand-in font, then jump to Slopper's own fonts a moment later and push the page around. The fonts now come from slopper.day itself and start loading with the page, so they're usually there before anything shows; on a slow connection the stand-in is sized to match, so the page stays put when they arrive.

changesets.summary: Set a goal in one screen: days first, then your pace
changesets.details: Setting a goal now starts with how many days you're in for (7, 14, 30, 100 or your own number), then offers four paces for those days: Safe, Getting there, Hardcore and Impossible, from one slop every five days to two a day. The goal is spelled out on flip tiles as you choose, and you can still type an exact number, name it or start another day. New accounts start here, and once the goal is set you're asked to share it, because saying it out loud makes you more likely to see it through.

changesets.summary: New API tokens stay hidden until you reveal them
changesets.details: A new token used to appear in full on Settings → API & MCP, and in the setup snippets below it, the moment you made it. It's now hidden behind dots, so it's safe to make one while sharing your screen or streaming. Copy it with the copy button, or press the eye to see it; the snippets show it only once it's revealed and always copy the real token.

changesets.summary: Auto-post only offers networks you can connect
changesets.details: Settings → Auto-post no longer shows X or LinkedIn with a "Not set up on this server" note. A network only appears once it can actually be connected.

changesets.summary: Only networks you can connect are mentioned
changesets.details: The homepage, the new-slop form, the update box and the agent guide said you could auto-post to X and LinkedIn even when they couldn't be connected. They now name only the networks that can be connected right now.

changesets.summary: Netlify environment sync sets every variable
changesets.details: netlify-cli 27 exits 0 without setting anything when `env:set` gets `--scope`, so the first sync reported 21 variables and set none. `vp run env:netlify` drops the flag, checks Netlify has every variable afterwards, and refuses a `SLOPPER_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY` that doesn't decode before it sets anything.

changesets.summary: Host on Netlify instead of Deno Deploy
changesets.details: Deno Deploy is being shut down, so slopper.day moves to Netlify. The React Router server builds into one Netlify Function and static files go to Netlify's CDN; `scripts/release.ts deploy` deploys Convex and then Netlify from this machine, and `publish` ends with it. Production variables are declared in `monosecret.toml` and `vp run env:netlify` sets them on Netlify, secrets read from one 1Password item. Deno is gone: `vp run start` and the e2e stack serve the build with Node (`scripts/serve.ts`). Screenshots are capped at 4 MB to fit Netlify's request limit.

changesets.summary: Serve robots.txt and the default share image
changesets.details: public/og.png, which every page without a screenshot names as its og:image, never existed, so shared links had no card. `node scripts/og-image.ts` now draws it from the site's fonts and colours. robots.txt keeps crawlers off /api/, /auth/ (each followed sign-in link starts a real OAuth flow) and /unsubscribe/; every rule ends in a slash so no profile URL is caught by a prefix.

changesets.summary: One countdown, the same for everyone
changesets.details: The header used to count down to midnight where you are while the race counted down to midnight UTC, so the same page showed two different times. Every clock now counts down to midnight UTC, when the race closes, so everyone sees the same time. Your goal days still end at your own midnight.

changesets.summary: Releases are pull requests, published from GitHub Actions
changesets.details: `vp exec monochange run release` commits the release on `chore/release`, pushes it through the pre-push CI and opens its pull request. Merging it runs `.github/workflows/release.yml`, which tags the release, deploys Convex and Netlify when the site is in it, and publishes released npm packages with npm trusted publishing. Every other push to main skips the workflow, and `monochange run publish` refuses to run outside it.

changesets.summary: Scheduled launches for agents
changesets.details: `create_slop` (and `POST /api/v1/slops`) takes `releaseAt`: "next" or an ISO 8601 date-time. New operations `list_scheduled`, `release_scheduled` and `cancel_scheduled` are on MCP and REST (`GET /api/v1/scheduled`, `POST /api/v1/scheduled/:id/release`, `DELETE /api/v1/scheduled/:id`). Queued launches live in the `scheduledLaunches` table; at `releaseAt` Convex puts each out through the same code as a launch made now, then calls `POST /api/scheduled/:id` so the app server runs the content check and the auto-post.

changesets.summary: Schedule launches from the CLI
changesets.details: `slopper launch --at next` (or `--at 2026-10-15T09:00`) schedules a launch instead of putting it out now. `slopper scheduled` lists what's waiting, `slopper release <id>` puts one out now and `slopper unschedule <id>` drops it. The skill explains when to line launches up.

changesets.summary: Schedule launches for later
changesets.details: Got three things ready at once? Throw one now and line the rest up. Pick "Next free day" and each goes out on the next day with nothing out or scheduled, right as that day's race starts, so it gets all 24 hours of votes. Or pick a day and time yourself. Nobody sees a scheduled slop until it goes out; then it counts towards your goal on that day and auto-posts if you asked. Your goal grid shows the days with something coming, and the new slop page lists what's waiting, with buttons to throw one now or unschedule it.

changesets.summary: Self-host fonts with preloads and matched fallbacks
changesets.details: Big Shoulders, Schibsted Grotesk and Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono come from `@fontsource-variable` packages and ship as hashed assets, instead of a render-blocking Google Fonts stylesheet that only then requested the files. The root route preloads the Latin faces of the two fonts every page opens with. `app.css` declares fallback faces built on Arial and Arial Narrow Bold with `size-adjust` and ascent/descent overrides (capitals, digits and the narrow 1 get their own), so a late swap measures at no layout shift on the homepage from 320px to 1440px. The content security policy no longer allows fonts.googleapis.com or fonts.gstatic.com.

changesets.summary: Shared links show a preview card
changesets.details: Links to slopper.day on X, LinkedIn, Bluesky and in chat apps now show Slopper's card instead of a bare link. A slop's own page still shows its first screenshot.

changesets.summary: Run Slopper from a terminal with the slopper CLI
changesets.details: Agents (and people) can launch, post updates, log money, check today's race and vote from a terminal with `npx @slopperday/cli`. The API page shows the command to sign it in with your token, and `slopper skill install` teaches your agents how to use it.

changesets.summary: Add the slopper CLI and its agent skill
changesets.details: `@slopperday/cli` maps every agent operation onto a command (`login`, `whoami`, `today`, `launch`, `edit`, `post`, `money`, `vote`, `upload`, `goal`, ...) and prints JSON. `@slopperday/skill` is the SKILL.md that explains it; `slopper skill` prints it and `slopper skill install` copies it into an agent's skills directory.

#### The CLI catches mistakes before sending anything, and never crashes on a bad config or network

_Owner:_ Ifiok Jr. · _Introduced in:_ 290c259

- `logout` and `skill` work with a broken config or an invalid `SLOPPER_URL`, so `slopper logout` can clear the config its own error message points at.
- An empty `SLOPPER_TOKEN` or `SLOPPER_URL` counts as unset instead of hiding the saved token or site.
- A reply that isn't JSON is an error, even a 200 from a site that isn't Slopper, so `login` never saves a token it couldn't check.
- `login` saves the site it checked the token on, `SLOPPER_URL` included, and makes an older, wider config owner-only before the token goes in.
- A connection that drops mid-reply, a config it can't read or a directory it can't create exits 1 with one line, not a stack trace.
- Stray words (`slopper post tiltmaze "Fixed it"`), `edit` with nothing to change, `post` without `--body`, `goal` without `--target` or `--days`, fractional or hex counts and amounts, and screenshots over 4 MB are usage mistakes (exit 2). Every usage mistake ends with the `slopper help` page to read.

### Documentation

- **Run the CLI with any package runner.** The README and the skill show `npx -y`, `pnpm dlx`, `bunx`, `yarn dlx -q`, `deno run -A npm:` and a global install, why npx needs `-y` (it waits on "Ok to proceed?" in a terminal) and yarn `-q` (its install log lands on stdout), and `SLOPPER_TOKEN` for agents that shouldn't write a config file.
